title: Corner Throw
description: A small now-playing cover resting in the corner of a warm white page, behaving like a picture-in-picture window. Throw it and it does not go where your finger let go: it projects the throw forward with the same deceleration a scroll view uses, picks the corner nearest to where that momentum would have carried it, and travels there on a spring that starts at your release velocity. While you hold it, a faint ghost waits in the corner it will land in, and changes its mind as your hand does. Catch it in flight and it stops in your fingers.
intent: Apple PiP corner projection, WWDC 2018 'Designing Fluid Interfaces' (https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2018/803/): the target is chosen from where the throw would land, not where the finger lifted, and the spring keeps the release velocity.
